rules.exemptions: Narrow exception for a town that accepts c.40P: voluntary-only regulation, not for owners of fewer than ten units or units with fair market rent above $400, owners compensated by the town
rules.interaction: Bars local rent control in Boston and Cambridge; statute text carries no effective date. The 2026 ballot question to repeal it (IP 25-21) was struck, see MA-02.
rules.title: State bar on local rent control (M.G.L. c.40P s.4)
rules.requirement: Massachusetts cities and towns may not enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, so there is no local rent cap in Boston or Cambridge. Massachusetts also has no statewide rent cap.
rules.key_value: Local rent control prohibited; no statewide cap
rules.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind

rules.coverage_conditions: Would have covered most residential rental units statewide
rules.exemptions: Proposed: owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, units under 10 years old, certain regulated units, short-term rentals, educational, religious or nonprofit facilities
rules.interaction: Supplemental source (no supplied D doc covers it; D059 was link-only): X023 for the petition number and terms, X007 (WBUR, 2026-06-23) and organizer test T5 for the struck status. Evidence that no rent cap applies in Boston or Cambridge; M.G.L. c.40P s.4 stays in force.
rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21, An Initiative Petition to Protect Tenants by Limiting Rent Increases (struck from 2026 ballot)
rules.requirement: A 2026 ballot question would have repealed the c.40P ban and capped annual rent increases. The Supreme Judicial Court removed it from the November 2026 ballot on 2026-06-23 (Cella v. Attorney General), so it is not law and no rent cap applies.
rules.key_value: Failed: proposed cap of the lesser of CPI or 5% never took effect
rules.quoted_span: The case, Cella v. Attorney General, SJC-13893 (embedded below), involved Initiative Petition 25-21

rules.exemptions: Leases or tenancies of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purposes
rules.interaction: Statewide; no Boston or Cambridge deposit rule found. Effective date is the 2025 c.9 amendment of clause (1)(b) (adds lessor's agents, fee in lieu of deposit capped with the deposit at 1 month's rent); the one-month cap itself is older.
rules.title: Security deposits (M.G.L. c.186 s.15B)
rules.requirement: A security deposit may not exceed the first month's rent. The landlord must give receipts and a statement of condition, hold the deposit in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, pay interest yearly and return it within 30 days with an itemized sworn list of any deductions; violations can cost three times the deposit.
rules.quoted_span: (iii) a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3)

rules.coverage_conditions: Lessors and agents of the lessor, at or before the start of a residential tenancy
rules.exemptions: Leases or tenancies of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purposes
rules.interaction: Same statute as the deposit rule (MA-03), recorded here for the upfront-charge limit; X022 (secondary) confirms landlords may not charge application fees. Current text of clause (1)(b) effective 2025-08-01 (2025 c.9). Broker fees are governed separately by M.G.L. c.112 s.87DDD1/2 (MA-05).
rules.title: Limit on upfront charges (M.G.L. c.186 s.15B(1)(b))
rules.requirement: At or before move-in, a landlord or the landlord's agent may charge only first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of up to one month's rent and the cost of a new lock and key. Application and screening fees charged by the landlord are not allowed.
rules.key_value: Only first month, last month, deposit, lock and key; no application fee
rules.quoted_span: (b) At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:

rules.coverage_conditions: Licensed brokers or salespersons finding rental housing for a fee
rules.interaction: Statute text marks this version as amended by 2025 c.9 s.43, effective August 1, 2025. Separate instrument from the c.186 s.15B upfront-charge limit (MA-04).
rules.title: Broker fee paid by the party who hired the broker (M.G.L. c.112 s.87DDD1/2)
rules.requirement: A rental broker works for either the tenant or the landlord, and any broker fee is paid only by the party who hired the broker, so a tenant does not pay a broker the landlord engaged.
rules.key_value: Broker fee paid only by the party that engaged the broker
rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson.

rules.interaction: Statewide floor; Boston and Cambridge add local source-of-income protections. No effective date in the text. Criminal-record screening is recorded separately under 803 CMR 5.00 (MA-12).
rules.title: Source of income and housing subsidy discrimination (M.G.L. c.151B s.4(10))
rules.requirement: A landlord may not discriminate against an applicant or tenant because they receive public assistance or a housing subsidy such as a Section 8 voucher, or because of the requirements of that program.
rules.key_value: No refusal based on public assistance or housing subsidy (vouchers)
rules.quoted_span: or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements, because the individual is such a recipient

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Department of Neighborhood Development)
rules.requirement: Housing providers with city (DND) funding or land, or with income-restricted inclusionary units, may not deny everyone with a criminal record and must decide case by case. They may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged convictions, juvenile records or convictions over 5 years old, and may not deny based on credit score.
rules.key_value: No blanket criminal-record ban; ignore non-conviction arrests, sealed and juvenile records, convictions over 5 years old
rules.citation: Boston DND Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017)
rules.quoted_span: Inclusionary Development Policy will not impose a blanket policy that denies

rules.coverage_conditions: Renting, buying, selling or financing housing in the City of Boston
rules.interaction: City web summary that names no ordinance section or date; enforced by the Boston Fair Housing Commission alongside M.G.L. c.151B s.4(10).
rules.title: Boston Fair Housing Regulations: rental assistance as a protected class
rules.requirement: Boston landlords may not refuse or treat renters differently because they use rental assistance such as Section 8, social security disability or veterans vouchers.
rules.key_value: No discrimination based on rental assistance (Section 8 and other vouchers)

rules.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance: source of income protection
rules.requirement: Cambridge landlords may not discriminate against renters based on source of income, including Section 8 and public benefits.
rules.key_value: Source of income (incl. Section 8, public benefits) protected
rules.quoted_span: Source of Income, includes Section 8 and public benefits

rules.title: Criminal record (CORI) checks for housing applicants (803 CMR 5.00)
rules.requirement: A landlord, property manager or real estate agent may request a standard criminal record (CORI) check only on the housing applicant and only as the final step of the application, and may not use it to screen other household members.
rules.key_value: CORI only as the final step of the application; applicant only
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords, property management companies and real estate agents evaluating applicants for market rate housing
rules.quoted_span: CORI shall only be requested for a housing applicant as the final step in the application process.
rules.interaction: Supplemental source: X029 (Cornell LII mirror of 803 CMR 5.04) because the supplied doc D056 was link-only (403). Effective date is the latest amendment shown (Mass Register Issue 1445, eff. 6/11/2021). Subsidized and public housing rules (5.05 and later) not read.

rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act (City of Boston Ordinances § 10-11.7)
rules.requirement: Any Boston landlord ending a tenancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources together with the notice to quit or notice of non-renewal, and send a copy of the notice to the city. Fines can reach $300 per day.
rules.key_value: Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources with every notice to quit or non-renewal
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords and foreclosing owners ending a tenancy or occupancy in Boston
rules.exemptions: Residences in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities, and non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities
rules.quoted_span: The Housing Stability Notification Act requires any landlord to provide renters with a Notice of Tenant’s Rights and Resources when planning to end a tenancy agreement.
rules.interaction: Notice-of-rights rule (the category covers notice); it does not limit the grounds for eviction, and Massachusetts has no just-cause statute. Effective 2020-11-06 per the city FAQ (D014).

rules.title: Tenants' Rights and Resources Notification Ordinance (Cambridge Mun. Code ch. 8.71)
rules.requirement: Cambridge landlords must give tenants the city's tenant rights and resources guide at the start of a tenancy and when taking steps to end it (notice to quit or summary process). Fines can reach $300 per day.
rules.key_value: Rights and resources guide at lease start and with notice to quit
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental agreements in Cambridge, including single units
rules.exemptions: Hospital, skilled nursing or health facility units, non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities, short-term rental units
rules.quoted_span: The Ordinance requires owners, landlords, and management companies to provide you with information at the start of your lease or tenancy as well as when your tenancy is being terminated.
rules.interaction: Notice-of-rights rule (the category covers notice); the city FAQ says it does not prevent an eviction otherwise allowed by law. No effective date in the source.

no_rule.note: Massachusetts has no statewide just-cause eviction statute: c.186 s.12 (D051) lets either party end a tenancy at will by written notice without cause; c.186 s.11 and s.31 (D050, D058) are notice-to-quit rules for nonpayment and s.18 (D053) is anti-retaliation, none limits the grounds for eviction.
